minor.issue: test_account_locks_after_five_failed_logins is flaky across runs: once the marketer account is locked, subsequent runs receive 429 on the first attempt instead of the 5 sequential 401s the test expects. Not a code bug; test should either (a) reset db.login_attempts for the target email first, or (b) use a throwaway email registered inside the test.

ui_bugs.issue: navigator.clipboard.writeText is awaited via a synchronous try/catch, so its Promise rejection (denied clipboard) becomes an unhandled rejection. In webpack dev, this triggers the red 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay which blocks the redeem button via pointer-events. In production the overlay does not show, but the unhandled rejection remains. Fix: use `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...).catch(()=>{})` (chain .catch on the Promise, don't wrap sync try/catch).

GET /api/coupons/{cid}/referrals allows any authenticated user in the workspace (including viewer) to see the leaderboard — intentional? Consider gating by role if the credit_owed number is sensitive.
Referral credit is written to stats.referral_credit via $inc but there is no UI surface showing this aggregate on the coupon (only the per-referrer leaderboard). Minor consistency gap.

rca of the issue: PublicCoupon.js: `try { navigator.clipboard.writeText(link); } catch { }` — this catches only synchronous throws, but writeText returns a Promise which rejects when clipboard permissions are denied. That rejection surfaces as an unhandled Promise rejection which webpack-dev-server catches and displays as a red overlay iframe over the entire page (id=webpack-dev-server-client-overlay). The overlay iframe then intercepts pointer events, breaking subsequent interactions like the Redeem button. Reproduction: open /c/SUMMER25?ref=alice-token in a browser context without clipboard-write permission, click Get link, then try to click Shop Now. Mitigation: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(link).catch(() => {})` on both PublicCoupon.js copyCode (line ~54-61) and generateShareLink (line ~63-70). No backend impact.
